newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen continuing rebound, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen continuing rebound, upside limited.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to continue their rebound on Wednesday but analysts said the market lacked the momentum to notch up signficant gains.

"I think following what happened in the U.S. overnight the Hong Kong market will still rebound today, but the upside is limited mostly because of the lack of turnover in the Hong Kong market," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities.
The Dow industrials rose 53.25 points overnight to close at 6,609.16. On Tuesday, the Hang Seng Index gained 110.73 points to 12,398.57.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London fell 19.72 points to 12,378.85.
"I think the market will open better but I would be surprised if it holds its gains. I would not want to be chasing prices at these levels," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"Turnover the last couple of days has been thin enough to doubt the rally," he said.
Chan said stocks were still vulnerable to U.S. economic data and the Hang Seng Index was likely to meet resistance at 12,500 points.
